text:
NEW YORK, NY / ACCESSWIRE / January 25, 2018 / Apple announced this week that the very first company store will be opened in Korea on Saturday. The company also said it is adding a new feature to iMessage allowing users to message businesses directly than call them. Shares of General Electric dropped after traders learned that the SEC is probing the company's accounting practices.
RDI Initiates Coverage on: 
Apple Inc.
https://rdinvesting.com/news/?ticker=AAPL 
General Electric Company
https://rdinvesting.com/news/?ticker=GE 
Apple Inc. shares closed down 1.59% on about 51 million shares traded on Wednesday. The tech giant is preparing to roll out a new feature on its iMessage that allows users to directly chat with businesses through the platform. It's called Business chat and will be debuting this spring. The feature was initially announced last year at the company's Worldwide Developer Conference and will launch with partners that include Wells Fargo and Discover. Despite this promising news, the stock closed in the red. Facebook commissioned a study by Nielsen that revealed last fall that a majority of customers would rather message a business than call its customer service number. 56% of the respondents had said they would rather text than phone. Apple also announced that the very first store in South Korea will be opening in Seoul this Saturday. Apple senior vice president of Retail, Angela Ahrendts commented, "We?re thrilled to open a new home for our customers in the vibrant city of Seoul and we look forward to continuing to grow in Korea. Our stores are gathering places for the community where everyone is welcome to connect, learn and create." The store will have the company's full line of products and as well as a collection of accessories.

General Electric Company shares closed down 2.66% on about 167 million shares traded yesterday. Trading volume was roughly double compared to usual as the stock dragged the Dow lower. It was revealed that the SEC is probing the company's accounting practices and is conducting "a deep review," that includes restating 2016 and 2017 financial results. The company's Chief Financial Officer Jamie Miller said, "We've been notified by the SEC that they are investigating the process leading to the insurance-reserve increase and fourth-quarter charge, as well as GE's revenue recognition and controls for long-term service agreements. We are cooperating fully with the investigation which is in very early stages." The company just posted quarterly results as well which included a $6.2 billion charge to the company's fourth quarter earnings. Jim Cramer of "The Street", who even owns GE, remarked, "This announcement immediately took steam out of the stock as it represents a headline risk into GE's practices, and we want to reiterate that this investigation reflects more on the previous management team who oversaw the company, and not the current regime. Accordingly, we do not hold [Chief Executive John] Flannery responsible for the past transgressions, but it is still up to him to move past the negative headlines through focus on the turnaround of the company and not the hand he was dealt."
